summary: _39. The Petitioner has further argued that the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court cancelling the coal block also qualifies as Change in Law under Article 10.1.1 (c) and Article 10.1.1 (d) of the PPA/PSA as a new condition of participation in the auction process for coal blocks under the Coal Block (Special Provisions) Act, 2015 has been prescribed. Clauses 10.1.1(c) and (d) of the PPA/PSA are extracted as under:_ _41. In view of the above, we hold that enactment of Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015 prescribing the auction route for allocation of coal block amounts to change in law if it affects the input cost of the Petitioner. However, in the present case, though the Petitioner participated in the auction process, it did not become successful and therefore the Petitioner cannot take the benefit of Article 10.1.1 (f) of the PPA._ 3. Aggrieved by the Commission`s said order dated 29.1.2020, the Petitioner and the Respondent, WBSEDCL, both approached the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (in short ‘APTEL’) through the Appeal Nos. 143/2020 and 66/2020, respectively. The Petitioner in Appeal No. 143/2020 had assailed the order of the Commission insofar as it held that the cancellation of allotment of the Ganeshpur Coal Block in pursuance of the judgment of the Hon`ble Supreme Court dated 25.08.2014 does not constitute a Change in Law event in terms of the PSA and PPA. The APTEL, vide the same judgment dated 3.9.2025, has held that the Commission has rightly held that the enactment of the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, constitutes a Change in Law under Article 10.1.1(f) of the PPA/PSA. However, the Commission has erred in holding that APNRL cannot take advantage of said Change in Law for the reason that APNRL, through its participation in the fresh bidding, did not become successful. The APTEL further held that the cancellation of allotment of the Ganeshpur captive coal block in pursuance of the coal block deallocation judgment of the Hon`ble Supreme Court constitutes a Change in Law event in terms of Article 10.1 (b) of the PPA/PSA executed between the parties. Therefore, APNRL is entitled to compensation for this effect. Accordingly, the APTEL allowed the Appeal filed by the Petitioner and remanded the matter with direction that the Petitioner is entitled for compensation Change in Law due to cancellation of coal block and to the extent of shortfall in the Tapering Linkage granted to it pending operationalization of the capital coal block, which it met through e-auction or import of coal etc. for generation of electricity in its power project and supply of the same to WBSEDCL. In Appeal No. 66/2022, WBSEDCL had assailed the order of the Commission in so far as (a) it holds that Ganeshpur Captive Coal Block allotted to APNRL is identified source of coal for the power project of APNRL in terms of PSA and PPA; and (b) it holds APNRL entitled to compensation for costs incurred for procuring coal from alternate sources on account 5. During the hearing on 18.9.2025, the learned counsel for the Petitioner has submitted that the Petitioner is in the process of compiling the computation of claims in terms of the judgment of APTEL and sought two weeks’ time to place on record the same. The learned counsel appearing for Respondent No. 1, i.e., WBSEDCL, voluminous details furnished by the Petitioner and to file a response thereon. Considering the request of the learned counsel for the Respondent, WBSEDCL, the Commission, while granting the last opportunity, permitted the Respondents to file their submissions to the Petitioner’s affidavit dated 4.10.2025 within two weeks. thereafter, i.e. from April 2019, being issued by a 3[rd] party agency, as appointed by the Petitioner. The Petitioner had raised Change in Law Claims (on account of changes in Taxes, Duties, etc.) for the same period against Respondent No. 1 herein in Petition Nos. 255/MP/2017 & 260/MP/2019. The data and values, concerning Change in Law claims which were raised in the said Petitions, had been ultimately referred for verification by the WBERC in its order dated 29.7.2022, passed in OA 417/22/23 to PFC Consulting Limited (‘PFCCL’), a public sector undertaking and a third party, who was jointly appointed by the parties. 10. During the course of the hearing, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, APNRL, made detailed submissions in response to the reply filed by the Respondent, 11. The matter was finally heard on 23.12.2025. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsels for the Petitioner and WBSEDCL made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments in the matter. The learned counsel for the PTC submitted that PTC is not willing to file the reply in the matter. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission permitted the parties to file their respective written submissions, if any. Subject to the above, the matter was reserved for order. 14. In view of the above, the Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation on account of Change in Law events under the present proceedings: with the reports thereafter, i.e. from April 2019, being by a 3[rd] party agency, as appointed by the Petitioner. 27 **.** _**Per Contra**_ , the Petitioner has submitted that Article 10.2 of the PPA requires that the affected party, on account of a Change in Law should be duly compensated, 31. Accordingly, Petition No. 305/MP/2015 is disposed of in terms of the above discussions and findings.
